items.s: Triggered when a customer deposits more than $10,000 in currency during a single business day.
items.w: A currency transaction report is triggered by cash deposits in excess of $10,000 in one business day.

items.s: Filed with FinCEN within 30 days after the suspicious activity is discovered.
items.w: Suspicious activity reports are filed with FinCEN within 30 days of discovering the suspicious activity.

items.s: A customer brings a $3,000 money order and an $8,000 traveler’s check to the firm on the same day.
items.w: Combined cash-type instruments of $11,000 in one day exceed $10,000, so a currency transaction report is filed.

items.s: A customer makes repeated $9,900 deposits that seem designed to stay just under the reporting threshold.
items.w: Deposits just under $10,000 are a listed red flag, so a suspicious activity report is the correct filing.

items.s: Must be filed with FinCEN within 15 days of the cash deposit.
items.w: The 15-day filing window applies to currency transaction reports, not to suspicious activity reports.

items.s: The representative is forbidden to tell the customer that this report has been filed.
items.w: A rep may never disclose to the customer that a suspicious activity report was filed about them.

items.s: A rep takes a second job managing an apartment building on weekends.
items.w: A second job away from the firm is an outside business activity, even though it involves no securities.

items.s: A rep helps a friend’s start-up raise capital by contacting the rep’s own clients on evenings.
items.w: Raising capital from clients for a deal the firm has not approved is selling away, a private securities transaction.

items.s: The rep must promptly update Form U4 after taking on the activity.
items.w: Outside business activity notice carries a requirement to promptly update the associated person’s Form U4.

items.s: The activity involves securities that the firm has not approved for sale or placed on its product list.
items.w: A private securities transaction involves securities not approved for sale by the firm, which is why it is called selling away.

items.s: A rep does consulting work on the side for a local business.
items.w: Side consulting is a listed example of an outside business activity requiring written notice to the firm.

items.s: If the firm approves the compensated deal, it must be recorded on the firm’s books and supervised like firm business.
items.w: An approved compensated private securities transaction must be on the books and records and supervised by the firm.

items.s: Correspondence is a written message sent to 25 or fewer persons within a 30-day period.
items.w: FINRA measures correspondence over a 30-calendar-day window, whereas the MSRB uses a longer 90-day window.

items.s: Correspondence is a written message sent to 25 or fewer persons within a 90-day period.
items.w: MSRB Rule G-21 defines correspondence using a 90-day period, which differs from the FINRA 30-day period.

items.s: Records of retail communications must be kept for three years after final use.
items.w: FINRA requires retail communication records, including approvals, to be retained three years after final use.

items.s: Records of advertising and advertising approvals must be kept for at least four years.
items.w: Municipal securities firms keep advertising records for four years under MSRB rules, one year longer than FINRA.

items.s: Communications are sorted into retail, correspondence, and institutional categories under Rule 2210.
items.w: FINRA Rule 2210 defines three types of communications with the public, based on audience and distribution numbers.

items.s: A newsletter or press release is an advertisement needing written principal approval, whether sent to retail or institutional investors.
items.w: MSRB rules do not distinguish retail from institutional audiences; any advertisement needs principal approval before first use.

title: MFP vs Firm or Its PAC (G-37)

items.s: May contribute up to $250 per election to a candidate the contributor is entitled to vote for.
items.w: The G-37 de minimis exception covers only MFPs giving $250 or less to candidates they can vote for.

items.s: Cannot make a political contribution of any amount to an issuer official without triggering the two-year ban.
items.w: The G-37 exception does not apply to the firm or a PAC controlled by it; no amount is permitted.

items.s: Includes municipal underwriters, traders, and their direct supervisors who deal with municipal issuers.
items.w: MFPs include associated persons in sales, trading, underwriting, and research for issuers, plus their direct supervisors.

items.s: A PAC controlled by the municipal securities firm gives $50 to an issuer official’s campaign.
items.w: A firm-controlled PAC has no exception, so even a small contribution triggers the two-year negotiated business ban.

items.s: May give $250 to the primary and another $250 to the general election for a candidate the contributor can vote for.
items.w: The $250 limit applies separately to each election, both the primary and the general, for an eligible voter.

items.s: The municipal securities firm itself gives $100 to the re-election campaign of an issuer’s mayor.
items.w: The $250 exception exists only for individual MFPs, so a contribution by the firm itself in any amount triggers the two-year ban.

items.s: A rep takes a weekend bartending job for extra income.
items.w: Under FINRA Rule 3270 an outside business activity requires written notice to the firm, not permission.

items.s: A rep wants to open a stock brokerage account at another firm.
items.w: Rule 3210 requires the employer’s prior written consent before an associated person opens an outside brokerage account.

items.s: A rep helps a friend’s start-up raise money from clients and will receive no compensation of any kind.
items.w: An uncompensated private securities transaction requires only notice, while any compensation would add the permission requirement.

items.s: A rep asks to be named trustee of a non-family customer’s trust.
items.w: Rule 3241 requires the firm to review and approve a rep serving as trustee for a non-family customer.

items.s: A rep prepares clients’ tax returns for a fee away from the firm.
items.w: Preparing tax returns for a fee is a listed outside business activity requiring notice to the employing firm.

items.s: A rep borrows money from a close friend who is a customer, based on their personal relationship.
items.w: A personal-relationship loan with a customer is permitted only with the firm’s prior written approval.
